item.title: Ram Sami strike enters fourth day, mediation set for Tuesday
item.description: NUW General Secretary and FTUC Secretary General Felix Anthony said the union had submitted its draft collective agreement more than two and a half years ago, but negotiations had failed to produce an agreement. Anthony said a meeting between the union, the employer and its legal adviser on September 3 lasted only four minutes.
item.content:encoded:
NUW General Secretary and FTUC Secretary General Felix Anthony said the union had submitted its draft collective agreement more than two and a half years ago, but negotiations had failed to produce an agreement.

Anthony said a meeting between the union, the employer and its legal adviser on September 3 lasted only four minutes.

He said the employer’s legal adviser informed the union that the company was not prepared to agree to anything beyond a “basic” agreement it had signed with another union.

“He further advised that if the Union was not happy with that, then the Union was free to take strike action,” Anthony said.

“The Union accepted the invitation to strike.”

Anthony said the company subsequently advised the Ministry of Employment that it intended to recruit workers to ensure operations continued.

He described the move as “scab labour” and accused the company of attempting to undermine workers exercising their legal right to strike.

“The decision to use ‘scab labour’ is a demonstration of bad faith and total denial of workers’ legitimate right to take strike action,” Anthony said.

“The intent is clear and that is to break the solidarity of workers and deny workers their rights.”

Around 40 Ram Sami and Sons workers are on strike over better working conditions, improved pay and recognition of their union as their representative.

Anthony also questioned the company’s recruitment of foreign workers.

He said the company had previously secured permits after telling the Immigration Department it could not find workers locally.

“There are about 10 or more foreign workers employed by Ram Sami and Sons,” he said.

“We now question as to the honesty of this employer claiming not to be able to find local workers but have absolutely no problem in recruiting them when workers exercise their legal right to strike.”

Anthony has called on the Immigration Department to rescind the company’s foreign worker permits and ensure local workers recruited during the dispute are given employment.

He also alleged that workers had previously been transported in the back of a truck used for chickens and had been expected to work in poor conditions.

“This exploitation must stop,” Anthony said.

The union has called for stronger labour laws to protect workers and said it would attend mediation talks called by the Ministry of Employment on Tuesday.

Anthony said the union remained hopeful the employer would genuinely engage in the mediation process and work towards resolving the dispute.

“We will attend in the hope that this employer will sincerely engage with the intent to resolve the impasse,” he said.

item.title: Opposition MP accuses Government of punishing teachers over ministry failures
item.description: Kumar said teachers were paid only up to Pay 18, with subsequent payments stopped following a Ministry audit that reportedly found some signed contracts had not been returned. “If this is the reason for stopping teachers’ salaries, then serious questions must be asked,” Kumar said.
item.content:encoded:
Kumar said teachers were paid only up to Pay 18, with subsequent payments stopped following a Ministry audit that reportedly found some signed contracts had not been returned.

“If this is the reason for stopping teachers’ salaries, then serious questions must be asked,” Kumar said.

“Where are the systems and people responsible for ensuring these contracts are properly processed?”

She questioned why administrative problems affecting teachers on a large scale were not identified and resolved earlier, given the Ministry’s existing hierarchy of heads of schools and divisional heads.

“Teachers should not be left without their salaries because of administrative failures within the Ministry,” she said.

Kumar also raised concerns about teachers who graduated in 2024 and applied for salary upgrades after completing their degrees.

She said these teachers had submitted their applications, degrees and university letters confirming completion of their studies, but were still waiting for payment.

Education Minister Aseri Radrodro has confirmed that 273 teachers are expected to be paid, subject to the availability of funds.

Kumar said teachers taking additional classes because of shortages were also carrying increased workloads while waiting for location allowances and salary upgrades.

She said teachers acting in higher positions were similarly waiting for acting allowances.

“Yet the Government continues to give teachers excuses by blaming the teachers for not submitting paperwork,” Kumar said.

Her comments follow previous concerns over salary arrears within the Ministry.

Kumar pointed to the announcement last month that salary arrears owed to 318 Ministry of Education staff were being expedited through Pay 17 and Pay 18.

She said the Ministry had previously attributed delays to internal processing and compliance requirements.

“The Fiji Teachers Association has also publicly raised concerns about salary and allowance delays affecting teachers who were forced to buy goods on credit because they were not paid by the ministry for months,” she said.

Kumar said the Government could not continue portraying teachers as responsible for administrative failures.

“Teachers should not become the scapegoats,” she said.

She acknowledged that teachers were required to comply with the Civil Service Code of Conduct and follow proper administrative procedures, but questioned what happened when those systems failed.

“What are teachers expected to do when their grievances are repeatedly ignored by the Ministry?” she asked.

Kumar also questioned the role of Employment Minister Agni Deo Singh, asking why he had not intervened on behalf of affected teachers.

“Workers’ rights cannot be selective. You cannot ignore workers at home, particularly teachers employed by the government,” she said.

She said teachers should not be portrayed as irresponsible when documentation may have already been submitted and was awaiting processing within the Ministry.

“If teachers have submitted all the required documentation and the paperwork is sitting somewhere within the Ministry, then the teachers should not be punished for the Ministry’s failure to process it,” Kumar said.

She called on Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka to intervene, saying the issue ultimately came down to leadership and accountability.

“If the Minister for Education cannot resolve something as fundamental as paying teachers correctly and on time, then the Prime Minister must ask whether the Minister for Education is capable of doing the job,” Kumar said.

“If the answer is no, then he should be replaced.”

item.title: RBF warns against unlicensed foreign exchange operators
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) has warned retail businesses, hotels and members of the public against engaging in foreign exchange activities without the required licence. The RBF says operating a foreign currency exchange business without a licence is a criminal offence and enforcement action will be taken against unauthorised operators.
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) has warned retail businesses, hotels and members of the public against engaging in foreign exchange activities without the required licence.

The RBF says operating a foreign currency exchange business without a licence is a criminal offence and enforcement action will be taken against unauthorised operators.

While hotels and relevant retail businesses may accept foreign currency from tourists as payment for goods and services, the RBF says strict conditions apply.

The transaction must be for the purchase of goods or services, any change given to the customer must be in Fijian dollars, and foreign currency received must be deposited with a commercial bank or sold to a restricted foreign exchange dealer within 30 days.

The RBF also clarified that businesses and individuals receiving foreign currency through legitimate transactions are prohibited from conducting further foreign exchange transactions or providing money-changing services to other customers.

Members of the public have been urged to use only licensed foreign exchange dealers.

The RBF says dealing with unlicensed operators exposes people to risks including fraud, loss of funds and a lack of legal protection.

Suspected unlicensed foreign exchange activities or other unauthorised financial services can be reported confidentially through the RBF’s Confidential Disclosures portal.

The central bank says it remains committed to protecting the integrity of Fiji’s financial system and safeguarding the interests of the public.

item.title: $90k boost
item.description: A $90,000 investment from the iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB) is set to expand a $500,000-plus tourism asset in Ra, as a locally-owned eco-tourism venture moves to increase its accommodation capacity. The loan, approved through TLTB’s Taukei Development Fund Facility, will finance the construction of two guest bure at Nanumi Au Eco Village in Navutulevu Village, Rakiraki.
item.content:encoded:
A $90,000 investment from the iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB) is set to expand a $500,000-plus tourism asset in Ra, as a locally-owned eco-tourism venture moves to increase its accommodation capacity.

The loan, approved through TLTB’s Taukei Development Fund Facility, will finance the construction of two guest bure at Nanumi Au Eco Village in Navutulevu Village, Rakiraki.

The expansion is expected to strengthen the venture’s ability to accommodate visitors and generate greater economic returns from the tourism lease while creating opportunities for the local community.

TLTB chief executive officer Solomone Nata formally handed over the loan agreement to Nanumi Au Eco Village director Kolinio Samuta, a member of mataqali Natilivaira, yavusa Natiliva of Navutulevu Village.

He said the investment demonstrated the potential for iTaukei entrepreneurs to turn customary land and local resources into viable businesses.

“This is one of the less common business ventures undertaken by iTaukei entrepreneurs, and I commend Mr Samuta for demonstrating the immense potential that exists within the eco-tourism sector,” Mr Nata said.

He said the initiative showed how indigenous communities could sustainably use their resources to create economic opportunities while protecting their cultural and environmental heritage.

Nanumi Au Eco Village has transformed land formerly used for sugar cane farming into a tourism destination offering cultural and nature-based experiences.

The venture operates largely on solar energy and offers village tours, mangrove exploration, waterfall and nature excursions, sevusevu and kava ceremonies, kayaking and other outdoor activities.

The name Nanumi Au, meaning ‘Remember Me’, reflects the venture’s focus on providing visitors with authentic Fijian cultural experiences while contributing to sustainable economic development in the community.

item.title: Digital push for SCGF
item.description: THE Sugar Cane Growers Fund (SCGF) is modernising its operations with new digital systems and an inclusion framework aimed at improving efficiency, accountability and access to services for sugarcane growers. SCGF chairman Marika Luveniyali said the launch of the Document Management System, SCGF Chatbot and Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Framework marked a significant ste
item.content:encoded:
THE Sugar Cane Growers Fund (SCGF) is modernising its operations with new digital systems and an inclusion framework aimed at improving efficiency, accountability and access to services for sugarcane growers.

SCGF chairman Marika Luveniyali said the launch of the Document Management System, SCGF Chatbot and Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Framework marked a significant step in the Fund’s institutional transformation.

Speaking at the launch in Lautoka on Thursday, Mr Luveniyali said the Document Management System would improve the way the Fund managed information, records, approvals and institutional knowledge.

He said the system would also provide growers with real-time access to information while strengthening accountability within the organisation.

“More importantly, it will strengthen accountability,” Mr Luveniyali said.

He said the Fund was also embracing artificial intelligence as part of its digital transformation strategy.

The SCGF Chatbot will improve access to information and services, reflecting the growing use of artificial intelligence across businesses and economies worldwide, he added.

“Artificial intelligence is no longer something that belongs only to large corporations or advanced economies.

“It is already changing the way people access information and services around the world, and SCGF is adopting the same approach.”

Mr Luveniyali said the GEDSI Framework was equally important to the Fund’s business operations because SCGF served a diverse group of growers.

The framework will help ensure gender equality, disability and social inclusion are considered in the development of the Fund’s policies, products and services.

“Our policies must recognise that diversity.”

Mr Luveniyali said the framework would provide a stronger foundation for the Fund to respond to the different circumstances and challenges faced by growers.

He acknowledged Business Link Pacific for providing technical support and guidance in developing the GEDSI Framework.

item.title: Council: Car buyers beware
item.description: MOTOR vehicle buyers must exercise extreme caution when purchasing vehicles from unauthorised dealers. The call from the Consumer Council of Fiji follows a string of complaints over poor after-sales service and alleged attempts to shift blame onto customers.
item.content:encoded:
MOTOR vehicle buyers must exercise extreme caution when purchasing vehicles from unauthorised dealers.

The call from the Consumer Council of Fiji follows a string of complaints over poor after-sales service and alleged attempts to shift blame onto customers.

Council chief executive officer Seema Shandil said at least 26 consumers had complained since 2020 about one particular dealer selling brand-new vehicles across multiple makes and brands.

She said investigations found the dealer lacked the technical expertise and spare parts needed to properly service or repair vehicles it sold.

“Consumers are paying substantial amounts for vehicles under the reasonable expectation of reliability and proper after-sales service,” Ms Shandil said.

“It is entirely unacceptable for a dealer to offload defective inventory, lack the basic capacity to repair what they sell, and then blame the customer when things go wrong.”

The council found a case where a consumer paid $66,888 for a 2018 twin-cab, only for its clutch system to fail shortly afterwards.

An independent inspection reportedly found second-hand parts had been fitted.

In another case, the council found a consumer paid $87,800 for a new 2025 SUV that developed water leakage, overheating and major engine failure.

Although the vehicle was repaired under warranty, the dealer maintained the damage was caused by driver negligence. She said the dispute remained unresolved over whether the problems were caused by product defects or driver misuse.

She urged buyers to verify the availability of qualified technicians, genuine spare parts and written warranty commitments before purchasing.

item.title: Group unveils plan
item.description: THE BSP Financial Group Limited has announced key executive leadership appointments within its Fiji operations, signalling a major push towards the long-term succession planning and regional corporate growth. Current BSP Life managing director Michael Nacola has been named to the newly-created position of Deputy Country Head for BSP Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
THE BSP Financial Group Limited has announced key executive leadership appointments within its Fiji operations, signalling a major push towards the long-term succession planning and regional corporate growth.

Current BSP Life managing director Michael Nacola has been named to the newly-created position of Deputy Country Head for BSP Fiji.

That appointment represents the group’s move to strengthen its succession planning across the group.

Relieving country head and head of Corporate and Institutional Banking for Fiji Maikash Ali will also take on an expanded leadership role as regional head of Corporate and Institutional Banking.

Mr Nacola has been the managing director of BSP Life in Fiji for the past seven years.

He will take on his new role reporting to BSP Fiji country head Haroon Ali once his successor is in place at BSP Life.

The bank stated it would conduct an internal and external search for Mr Nacola’s replacement at BSP Life.

item.title: Kanda to serve second term
item.description: Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda will serve a second term in the position – following unanimous support from members of the board of governors voting in a recent election. “I am deeply honoured by the trust our members have placed in me at this critical moment in our region’s history,” Ms Kanda said in a statement from the ADB.
item.content:encoded:
Asian Development Bank (ADB) president Masato Kanda will serve a second term in the position – following unanimous support from members of the board of governors voting in a recent election.

“I am deeply honoured by the trust our members have placed in me at this critical moment in our region’s history,” Ms Kanda said in a statement from the ADB.

“New shocks are striking Asia and the Pacific, even before economies have recovered from the last, and the international order is under its greatest strain in generations.”

Mr Kanda said the ADB must be the region’s anchor of stability.

However, he added stability could not mean standing still.

“We must mobilise with speed and at the scale our members need, to protect people today while helping build a brighter future for the next generation.”

Mr Kanda was first elected as ADB 11th president on November 27 in 2024 and assumed the position on February 24 last year, serving the remaining term of his predecessor, Masatsugu Asakawa.

According to the ADB, ADB has significantly expanded its support to members during a period of overlapping crises since taking up office.

The ADB is a leading multilateral development bank supporting sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth across Asia and the Pacific.

In 2025, it provided a record $44 billion in support, including more than $29b from its own resources and nearly $15b in cofinancing.

Mr Kanda’s new term runs for five years beginning November 24 later this year.
